title: Arterial Windlass Tourniquet - Femoral Bleed (Variation 1 - Upper Extremity)
trigger_symptoms: arterial thigh wound in Sector A
blood spurting from upper leg in Sector A
deep leg gash pumping blood in Sector A
arterial bleed thigh in Sector A
steps: Wrap broad cloth 2-3 inches above thigh wound.
Tie half knot, place rigid stick on knot.
Tie full knot over stick.
Twist stick until all bright red spurting stops completely.
Secure stick ends firmly with cloth.
Write exact tourniquet time on forehead.
warnings: NEVER use thin wire or shoelaces (cuts nerves and skin).
DO NOT loosen tourniquet once placed.
summary: Immediate windlass tourniquet for massive femoral arterial bleed using cloth and stick. Tailored for field triage.

title: Direct Pressure & Elevation - Deep Forearm Laceration (Variation 2 - Lower Extremity)
trigger_symptoms: deep arm cut bleeding heavily in ruined building
forearm gash steady blood flow in ruined building
cut wrist bleeding but not spurting in ruined building
steps: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with cleanest cloth available.
Maintain pressure without lifting cloth to check for 10 full minutes.
Elevate forearm above heart level.
Add more cloth on top if blood soaks through; never remove base layer.
warnings: DO NOT remove blood-soaked base gauze.
Avoid tourniquet if steady venous bleeding stops with pressure.
summary: Direct continuous pressure and limb elevation for deep venous bleeding. Tailored for rubble rescue.

title: Junctional Axillary Wound Packing - Armpit / Shoulder (Variation 3 - Groin)
trigger_symptoms: bleeding deep in armpit in flood evacuation
shoulder junction wound bleeding in flood evacuation
shrapnel in armpit pumping blood in flood evacuation
steps: Tourniquets cannot fit here; pack cloth tightly into the wound cavity directly against the bleeding vessel.
Use fingers to push cloth into deepest point of bleed.
Apply hard direct pressure with both hands for at least 3 to 5 minutes.
Wrap bandage around chest and shoulder to hold pressure.
warnings: DO NOT leave junctional wound loose; continuous cavity packing is required.
summary: Deep cavity packing for junctional axillary hemorrhage where tourniquets cannot be applied. Tailored for isolated shelter.

title: Sucking Chest Wound - 3-Sided Flutter Valve Seal (Variation 4 - Torso)
trigger_symptoms: hissing chest wound in collapsed doorway
air bubbling from rib puncture in collapsed doorway
sucking sound when breathing in collapsed doorway
chest wall puncture in collapsed doorway
steps: Immediately cover hole with clean plastic wrap or heavy plastic bag.
Tape plastic down on THREE sides only, leaving the bottom side open.
The 3-sided seal lets trapped air escape during exhalation, preventing tension pneumothorax.
If victim worsens, momentarily lift seal to burp trapped air.
warnings: DO NOT tape all 4 sides without a flutter valve; air pressure will collapse lung.
summary: Improvised 3-sided occlusive flutter valve seal for open pneumothorax. Tailored for flood zone.

title: Blast Impalement - Stabilizing Impaled Rebar / Metal (Variation 5 - Neck)
trigger_symptoms: metal rod stuck in thigh in Sector A
rebar impaled in abdomen in Sector A
piece of metal sticking out of leg in Sector A
knife stuck in back in Sector A
steps: DO NOT PULL THE OBJECT OUT. It is plugging severed blood vessels.
Place bulky rolled cloth on BOTH sides of the object to prevent movement.
Bandage securely around the object without putting pressure directly down on it.
Keep victim completely still and calm.
warnings: NEVER attempt to extract an impaled object in the field; causes fatal hemorrhage.
summary: Field stabilization of impaled debris using bilateral bulky support bandages. Tailored for field triage.

title: Traumatic Limb Amputation - Stump Tourniquet & Part Preservation (Variation 6 - Scalp)
trigger_symptoms: hand severed by machinery in ruined building
foot amputated by collapsed wall in ruined building
leg severed below knee in ruined building
steps: Apply high-and-tight windlass tourniquet immediately on the remaining stump.
Wrap the stump in clean cloth.
Retrieve severed body part; wrap in clean dry cloth.
Place wrapped part inside a sealed dry plastic bag.
Place bag into cool water with ice if available. NEVER submerge part directly in water.
warnings: DO NOT place severed limb directly on ice or in water without a protective dry bag.
summary: Stump hemorrhage arrest and dry-sealed cold preservation of amputated limbs. Tailored for rubble rescue.

title: Abdominal Evisceration - Protruding Organs Care (Variation 7 - Upper Extremity)
trigger_symptoms: stomach sliced open intestines out in flood evacuation
belly wound guts protruding in flood evacuation
abdominal blast wound organs visible in flood evacuation
steps: DO NOT attempt to push intestines or organs back inside.
Cover protruding organs with a clean, moist plastic wrap or clean plastic sheet.
Keep victim lying on back with knees bent up to reduce abdominal wall tension.
Prevent hypothermia by insulating torso with blankets over the plastic.
warnings: NEVER apply dry gauze directly to organs (causes tissue tearing and shock).
summary: Moist plastic occlusive barrier and flexed-knee positioning for abdominal evisceration. Tailored for isolated shelter.

title: Scalp Laceration - High Volume Capillary Bleeding (Variation 8 - Lower Extremity)
trigger_symptoms: head cut bleeding everywhere in collapsed doorway
scalp wound bleeding profusely in collapsed doorway
blood dripping down face from forehead in collapsed doorway
steps: Check for depressed skull fracture (soft dent). If bone is firm, apply direct pressure with flat cloth.
Wrap bandana or t-shirt firmly around head like a sweatband.
Keep victim sitting upright to reduce cranial venous pressure.
warnings: DO NOT press deeply if you feel skull bone fragments or soft depressed spots.
summary: Broad circumference head wrap for profuse capillary scalp lacerations. Tailored for flood zone.

If victim worsens, momentarily lift seal to burp trapped air.
warnings: DO NOT tape all 4 sides without a flutter valve; air pressure will collapse lung.
summary: Improvised 3-sided occlusive flutter valve seal for open pneumothorax. Tailored for flood zone.

title: Blast Impalement - Stabilizing Impaled Rebar / Metal (Variation 45 - Groin)
trigger_symptoms: metal rod stuck in thigh in Sector A
rebar impaled in abdomen in Sector A
piece of metal sticking out of leg in Sector A
knife stuck in back in Sector A
steps: DO NOT PULL THE OBJECT OUT. It is plugging severed blood vessels.
Place bulky rolled cloth on BOTH sides of the object to prevent movement.
Bandage securely around the object without putting pressure directly down on it.
Keep victim completely still and calm.
warnings: NEVER attempt to extract an impaled object in the field; causes fatal hemorrhage.
summary: Field stabilization of impaled debris using bilateral bulky support bandages. Tailored for field triage.

title: Traumatic Limb Amputation - Stump Tourniquet & Part Preservation (Variation 46 - Torso)
trigger_symptoms: hand severed by machinery in ruined building
foot amputated by collapsed wall in ruined building
leg severed below knee in ruined building
steps: Apply high-and-tight windlass tourniquet immediately on the remaining stump.
Wrap the stump in clean cloth.
Retrieve severed body part; wrap in clean dry cloth.
Place wrapped part inside a sealed dry plastic bag.
Place bag into cool water with ice if available. NEVER submerge part directly in water.
warnings: DO NOT place severed limb directly on ice or in water without a protective dry bag.
summary: Stump hemorrhage arrest and dry-sealed cold preservation of amputated limbs. Tailored for rubble rescue.

title: Abdominal Evisceration - Protruding Organs Care (Variation 47 - Neck)
trigger_symptoms: stomach sliced open intestines out in flood evacuation
belly wound guts protruding in flood evacuation
abdominal blast wound organs visible in flood evacuation
steps: DO NOT attempt to push intestines or organs back inside.
Cover protruding organs with a clean, moist plastic wrap or clean plastic sheet.
Keep victim lying on back with knees bent up to reduce abdominal wall tension.
Prevent hypothermia by insulating torso with blankets over the plastic.
warnings: NEVER apply dry gauze directly to organs (causes tissue tearing and shock).
summary: Moist plastic occlusive barrier and flexed-knee positioning for abdominal evisceration. Tailored for isolated shelter.

title: Scalp Laceration - High Volume Capillary Bleeding (Variation 48 - Scalp)
trigger_symptoms: head cut bleeding everywhere in collapsed doorway
scalp wound bleeding profusely in collapsed doorway
blood dripping down face from forehead in collapsed doorway
steps: Check for depressed skull fracture (soft dent). If bone is firm, apply direct pressure with flat cloth.
Wrap bandana or t-shirt firmly around head like a sweatband.
Keep victim sitting upright to reduce cranial venous pressure.
warnings: DO NOT press deeply if you feel skull bone fragments or soft depressed spots.
summary: Broad circumference head wrap for profuse capillary scalp lacerations. Tailored for flood zone.

title: Arterial Windlass Tourniquet - Femoral Bleed (Variation 49 - Upper Extremity)
trigger_symptoms: arterial thigh wound in Sector A
blood spurting from upper leg in Sector A
deep leg gash pumping blood in Sector A
arterial bleed thigh in Sector A
steps: Wrap broad cloth 2-3 inches above thigh wound.
Tie half knot, place rigid stick on knot.
Tie full knot over stick.
Twist stick until all bright red spurting stops completely.
Secure stick ends firmly with cloth.
Write exact tourniquet time on forehead.
warnings: NEVER use thin wire or shoelaces (cuts nerves and skin).
DO NOT loosen tourniquet once placed.
summary: Immediate windlass tourniquet for massive femoral arterial bleed using cloth and stick. Tailored for field triage.

title: Direct Pressure & Elevation - Deep Forearm Laceration (Variation 50 - Lower Extremity)
trigger_symptoms: deep arm cut bleeding heavily in ruined building
forearm gash steady blood flow in ruined building
cut wrist bleeding but not spurting in ruined building
steps: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with cleanest cloth available.
Maintain pressure without lifting cloth to check for 10 full minutes.
Elevate forearm above heart level.
Add more cloth on top if blood soaks through; never remove base layer.
warnings: DO NOT remove blood-soaked base gauze.
Avoid tourniquet if steady venous bleeding stops with pressure.
summary: Direct continuous pressure and limb elevation for deep venous bleeding. Tailored for rubble rescue.

title: Hands-Only Adult CPR (100-120 bpm Continuous) (Protocol 1)
trigger_symptoms: adult collapsed not breathing in evacuation center
man passed out no pulse in evacuation center
woman unresponsive not breathing in evacuation center
cardiac arrest victim in evacuation center
steps: Check consciousness: Shake shoulders and shout.
Check breathing: Look for chest rising for 5 seconds. If NOT breathing, start immediately.
Heel of hand in center of chest, other hand interlaced.
Lock elbows, push hard and fast 2 inches deep at 100-120 bpm (beat of 'Stayin Alive').
Allow full chest recoil. Do not stop until help arrives.
warnings: DO NOT perform compressions if casualty is responsive or breathing normally.
Hands-only is safer and continuous; do not interrupt for untrained rescue breaths.
summary: Continuous adult chest compressions at 100-120 bpm cadence. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Infant CPR (Gentle 2-Finger Compressions) (Protocol 2)
trigger_symptoms: baby not breathing in flooded house
infant limp and blue lips in flooded house
newborn unresponsive in flooded house
infant choking then stopped breathing in flooded house
steps: Tap soles of baby's feet and call name.
Check chest rise for 5 seconds. If not breathing, place baby on flat table or firm floor.
Place 2 fingers in center of chest just below nipple line.
Compress gently 1.5 inches deep at 100-120 bpm.
Give 2 gentle puffs of air covering both mouth and nose every 30 compressions.
warnings: DO NOT use adult two-handed force on an infant (breaks sternum and ribs).
summary: Pediatric two-finger 1.5-inch compressions for infant cardiopulmonary arrest. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Conscious Adult Choking - Heimlich Abdominal Thrusts (Protocol 3)
trigger_symptoms: cannot speak or cough clutching throat in collapsed cellar
adult choking on food in collapsed cellar
silent choking hands at throat in collapsed cellar
steps: Ask: 'Are you choking? Can you speak?'. If they cannot speak, act immediately.
Stand behind victim, wrap arms around waist.
Make a fist with one hand, place thumb side just above navel.
Grasp fist with other hand and thrust inward and upward forcefully.
Repeat thrusts until object is expelled or victim goes unconscious.
warnings: DO NOT slap back of a choking adult while they are standing upright (can wedge object deeper).
summary: Inward-upward subdiaphragmatic abdominal thrusts for acute foreign body airway obstruction. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Conscious Infant Choking (5 Back Blows + 5 Chest Thrusts) (Protocol 4)
trigger_symptoms: baby choking silent gasping in rubble area
infant swallowed small toy choking in rubble area
infant turned purple gasping in rubble area
steps: Lay infant face down along your forearm, supporting head with your hand.
Keep baby's head lower than their chest.
Deliver 5 firm back blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand.
Flip baby face up onto other forearm.
Deliver 5 quick chest thrusts with 2 fingers.
Repeat until airway clears.
warnings: DO NOT perform blind finger sweeps in baby's mouth (pushes foreign object into larynx).
summary: Alternating back blows and chest thrusts for acute infant airway obstruction. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Near-Drowning / Submersion Rescue Airway Clearing (Protocol 5)
trigger_symptoms: pulled from flood water unconscious in evacuation center
near drowning victim not breathing in evacuation center
submerged in water swallowed silt in evacuation center
steps: Place casualty flat on back on firm ground.
Tilt head back gently to open airway; clear mud/silt from mouth with cloth.
If not breathing, deliver 5 initial rescue breaths to oxygenate lungs.
Begin 30 chest compressions followed by 2 breaths.
Do not pause; hypothermic drowning victims can recover after prolonged CPR.
warnings: DO NOT squeeze stomach or invert victim to drain water (causes fatal vomit aspiration).
summary: Hypothermic drowning airway clearance and combined rescue breath CPR. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Smoke Inhalation & Carbon Monoxide Exposure (Protocol 6)
trigger_symptoms: coughing black soot from fire in flooded house
trapped in smoky room dizzy in flooded house
smoke inhalation burning throat in flooded house
steps: Evacuate victim immediately into open fresh air.
Position seated upright to maximize lung volume.
Place a damp cloth over mouth to filter remaining ambient smoke.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
Monitor for airway swelling (stridor/wheezing).
warnings: DO NOT keep victim lying flat (worsens pulmonary edema).
summary: Fresh air evacuation, upright tripod positioning, and humidified airway protection for smoke victims. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Smoke Inhalation & Carbon Monoxide Exposure (Protocol 36)
trigger_symptoms: coughing black soot from fire in rubble area

steps: Evacuate victim immediately into open fresh air.
Position seated upright to maximize lung volume.
Place a damp cloth over mouth to filter remaining ambient smoke.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest.
Monitor for airway swelling (stridor/wheezing).
warnings: DO NOT keep victim lying flat (worsens pulmonary edema).
summary: Fresh air evacuation, upright tripod positioning, and humidified airway protection for smoke victims. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Hands-Only Adult CPR (100-120 bpm Continuous) (Protocol 37)
trigger_symptoms: adult collapsed not breathing in evacuation center
man passed out no pulse in evacuation center
woman unresponsive not breathing in evacuation center
cardiac arrest victim in evacuation center
steps: Check consciousness: Shake shoulders and shout.
Check breathing: Look for chest rising for 5 seconds. If NOT breathing, start immediately.
Heel of hand in center of chest, other hand interlaced.
Lock elbows, push hard and fast 2 inches deep at 100-120 bpm (beat of 'Stayin Alive').
Allow full chest recoil. Do not stop until help arrives.
warnings: DO NOT perform compressions if casualty is responsive or breathing normally.
Hands-only is safer and continuous; do not interrupt for untrained rescue breaths.
summary: Continuous adult chest compressions at 100-120 bpm cadence. Field standard compliant with IFRC 2025 guidelines.

title: Infant CPR (Gentle 2-Finger Compressions) (Protocol 38)
trigger_symptoms: baby not breathing in flooded house

steps: Tap soles of baby's feet and call name.

Place 2 fingers in center of chest just below nipple line.

title: Conscious Adult Choking - Heimlich Abdominal Thrusts (Protocol 39)
trigger_symptoms: cannot speak or cough clutching throat in collapsed cellar

Grasp fist with other hand and thrust inward and upward forcefully.
Repeat thrusts until object is expelled or victim goes unconscious.

title: Cervical Spine Stabilization - Rubble Fall (Case 1)
trigger_symptoms: fell from roof neck pain - left limb
hit on head by concrete cannot feel toes - left limb
spinal injury tingling hands - left limb
steps: Tell victim: 'DO NOT MOVE YOUR HEAD'.
Kneel at top of victim's head; place hands firmly on both sides of head to hold in-line position.
Place rolled jackets or shoes on both sides of head to immobilize.
Do not move victim unless rising flood or active fire forces immediate relocation.
warnings: DO NOT turn victim's head to the side or allow neck bending.
summary: In-line cervical manual immobilization and bilateral head blocks. Aligned with FEMA CERT field operating standards.

title: Closed Femur Thigh Fracture - Anatomic Splinting (Case 2)
trigger_symptoms: thigh bent unnatural angle severe pain - right limb
broken thigh bone cannot stand - right limb
femur fracture deformed leg - right limb
steps: Gently support the injured leg in position found.
Place a folded blanket or cloth between both legs for padding.
Bind the uninjured leg to the broken leg using cloth ties above and below fracture.
Check toes for warmth and pulse after tying.
warnings: DO NOT try to forcefully straighten or snap the bone back into place.
summary: Anatomic leg-to-leg traction splinting for closed femur fractures. Aligned with FEMA CERT field operating standards.

title: Open Compound Fracture - Bone Protruding (Case 3)
trigger_symptoms: broken arm bone sticking out of skin - lower body
bone pierced through leg bleeding - lower body
compound fracture exposed bone - lower body
steps: Control bleeding by pressing around the bone perimeter, NEVER press directly on bone.
Cover exposed bone with clean, moist cloth.
Immobilize joints above and below fracture with rigid cardboard or sticks.
Secure splint snugly without cutting off blood flow.
warnings: NEVER push the protruding bone back inside the skin (introduces deadly bacteria).
summary: Perimeter hemorrhage control, moist bone shielding, and rigid splinting for compound fractures. Aligned with FEMA CERT field operating standards.

title: Pelvic Fracture Stabilization - Improvised Pelvic Binder (Case 4)
trigger_symptoms: hit by falling wall pelvic pain - upper body
cannot walk hips feel crushed - upper body
severe groin pain after collapse - upper body
steps: Slide a wide bedsheet or jacket under victim's pelvis.
Cross ends over front of pelvis and pull tight to compress pelvic ring together.
Tie tightly or clamp with safety pins.
Tie knees and ankles together with cloth to prevent hip rotation.
warnings: DO NOT rock or press down on hips to 'test' stability (triggers internal hemorrhage).
summary: Circumferential pelvic sheet compression binder to control internal retroperitoneal bleeding. Aligned with FEMA CERT field operating standards.

title: Crush Syndrome & Entrapment Extrication Protocol (Case 5)
trigger_symptoms: legs pinned under concrete slab for 2 hours - left limb
crushed by heavy beam rescued - left limb
trapped under masonry long time - left limb
steps: Prolonged crushing traps potassium and toxins in limbs; sudden release can cause cardiac arrest.

Monitor heart rhythm and urine output.
warnings: DO NOT apply tight tourniquets unless catastrophic arterial bleeding occurs upon slab removal.
summary: Systemic hydration and reperfusion hyperkalemia mitigation for crush syndrome victims. Aligned with FEMA CERT field operating standards.

title: Second & Third Degree Fire Burns - Clean Water Cooling (Variant 2)
trigger_symptoms: severe burns skin blistered in relief camp kitchen
clothing caught fire burned chest in relief camp kitchen
charred black skin from explosion in relief camp kitchen
steps: Cool burned area immediately under clean, room-temperature running water for 10-20 minutes.
Gently remove jewelry or loose clothing before swelling begins.
DO NOT peel clothing melted onto burn.
Cover loosely with clean plastic wrap or dry lint-free cloth.
Keep victim warm to avoid hypothermia.
warnings: NEVER apply butter, oil, grease, toothpaste, or ice (causes severe infection and tissue death).
DO NOT pop burn blisters.
summary: Thermal burn cooling, barrier plastic occlusive dressing, and systemic hypothermia prevention. Adheres to WHO Burn Management Guidelines.

title: Chemical Splash to Eyes - Copious Irrigation (Variant 3)

Cover with clean cloth after flushing.
warnings: DO NOT rub eye; DO NOT attempt to neutralize acid with alkaline solutions.
summary: Emergency 20-minute ocular chemical dilution and lateral drainage. Adheres to WHO Burn Management Guidelines.

title: Severe Hypothermia Stage 2/3 - Passive Core Rewarming (Scenario 1)
trigger_symptoms: shivering stopped confused cold - coastal zone
hypothermia pale blue lips drowsy - coastal zone
stuck in freezing flood water hours - coastal zone
steps: Handle victim with extreme gentleness; rough movement can trigger fatal ventricular fibrillation.
Gently cut away all wet clothing.
Wrap core (chest, neck, groin, head) in dry sleeping bag, blankets, and plastic barrier.
Place insulating layer between victim and cold ground.
Give warm sweet drinks ONLY if fully conscious and swallowing.
warnings: DO NOT rub arms and legs. DO NOT give alcohol. DO NOT immerse in hot bath (causes afterdrop).
summary: Gentle passive core rewarming and ground insulation for deep hypothermia. Complies with Wilderness Medical Society protocols.

title: Heatstroke Emergency - Rapid Active Evaporative Cooling (Scenario 2)
trigger_symptoms: hot dry skin no sweat confused - mountain camp
heatstroke passed out fever - mountain camp
high fever delirious in hot sun - mountain camp
steps: Move victim into shade immediately.
Remove outer clothing.
Douse body with cool water and fan vigorously to create rapid evaporative cooling.
Apply cool wet packs to neck, armpits, and groin.
Stop cooling once skin feels cool to touch to prevent shivering.
warnings: DO NOT give aspirin or acetaminophen (does not reduce environmental hyperthermia, damages liver).
summary: Active evaporative cooling and high-flow circulatory ice/wet packs for heatstroke. Complies with Wilderness Medical Society protocols.

title: Trench Foot / Immersion Foot - Prolonged Flood Exposure (Scenario 3)
trigger_symptoms: feet numb white wrinkled in flood water - urban flash flood
painful swollen feet standing in water - urban flash flood
trench foot red blisters - urban flash flood
steps: Remove wet boots and socks immediately.
Gently wash feet with clean water.
Dry thoroughly, especially between toes.
Elevate feet and keep warm and exposed to dry air.
Never walk on affected feet until sensation returns.
warnings: DO NOT apply direct intense heat (stoves/fire); burns numb skin without feeling.
summary: Drying, limb elevation, and gradual rewarming for flood-immersion trench foot. Complies with Wilderness Medical Society protocols.

title: Lightning Strike Mass Casualty - Reverse Triage (Scenario 4)

Check for secondary blast injuries and ruptured eardrums.
warnings: DO NOT assume a motionless lightning victim is dead; immediate CPR has high survival rate.
summary: Reverse triage prioritization and immediate resuscitative CPR for lightning strike victims. Complies with Wilderness Medical Society protocols.

steps: Reverse triage rule: Victims who look dead (in cardiac/respiratory arrest) must be treated FIRST.

title: Severe Hypothermia Stage 2/3 - Passive Core Rewarming (Scenario 33)
trigger_symptoms: shivering stopped confused cold - coastal zone
hypothermia pale blue lips drowsy - coastal zone
stuck in freezing flood water hours - coastal zone
steps: Handle victim with extreme gentleness; rough movement can trigger fatal ventricular fibrillation.
Gently cut away all wet clothing.
Wrap core (chest, neck, groin, head) in dry sleeping bag, blankets, and plastic barrier.
Place insulating layer between victim and cold ground.
Give warm sweet drinks ONLY if fully conscious and swallowing.
warnings: DO NOT rub arms and legs. DO NOT give alcohol. DO NOT immerse in hot bath (causes afterdrop).
summary: Gentle passive core rewarming and ground insulation for deep hypothermia. Complies with Wilderness Medical Society protocols.

title: Heatstroke Emergency - Rapid Active Evaporative Cooling (Scenario 34)
trigger_symptoms: hot dry skin no sweat confused - mountain camp
heatstroke passed out fever - mountain camp
high fever delirious in hot sun - mountain camp
steps: Move victim into shade immediately.
Remove outer clothing.
Douse body with cool water and fan vigorously to create rapid evaporative cooling.
Apply cool wet packs to neck, armpits, and groin.
Stop cooling once skin feels cool to touch to prevent shivering.
warnings: DO NOT give aspirin or acetaminophen (does not reduce environmental hyperthermia, damages liver).
summary: Active evaporative cooling and high-flow circulatory ice/wet packs for heatstroke. Complies with Wilderness Medical Society protocols.

title: Trench Foot / Immersion Foot - Prolonged Flood Exposure (Scenario 35)
trigger_symptoms: feet numb white wrinkled in flood water - urban flash flood

Elevate feet and keep warm and exposed to dry air.
Never walk on affected feet until sensation returns.

title: Neurotoxic Elapid Snakebite (Cobra / Krait) - Pressure Immobilization (Profile 1)
trigger_symptoms: cobra bite leg dropping eyelids in rural sector
snake bite difficulty breathing drowsy in rural sector
krait bite painless puncture in rural sector
steps: Keep victim completely immobile and calm.
Apply broad pressure bandage firmly over bite site and up the entire limb (tension of a sprained ankle wrap).
Splint limb to prevent joint movement.
Prepare for mouth-to-mouth rescue breaths if breathing fails.
warnings: DO NOT cut, suck, wash bite site, or apply ice/tourniquets.
summary: Lymphatic pressure immobilization and respiratory vigilance for neurotoxic envenomation. Aligned with WHO Envenomation Guidelines.

title: Viperid Hemotoxic Snakebite - Local Swelling & Splinting (Profile 2)
trigger_symptoms: viper bite extreme swelling bleeding in temporary shelter
snake bite severe localized pain purple skin in temporary shelter
steps: Keep casualty still; elevate limb slightly if swelling is rapid.
Immobilize limb with splint without tight constrictive wrapping.
Remove rings and tight clothing before massive swelling.
Mark boundary of swelling with pen every 15 minutes.
warnings: DO NOT apply high-pressure tourniquets (causes localized gangrene with viper venom).
summary: Limb immobilization, progressive swelling tracking, and ring removal for viper bites. Aligned with WHO Envenomation Guidelines.

title: Wild Mushroom / Plant Poisoning - Ingestion Triage (Profile 3)
trigger_symptoms: ate wild mushrooms vomiting stomach pain in flood forest
child ate toxic berries convulsions in flood forest
poisonous plant poisoning in flood forest
steps: Save a sample of the mushroom or plant for identification.
If within 1 hour and victim is fully alert, give activated charcoal in water if available.
Maintain hydration with small sips of clean water.
Position on side to prevent choking if vomiting.
warnings: DO NOT induce vomiting with salt water or ipecac (causes lung aspiration and electrolyte collapse).
summary: Specimen retention, gastric toxin absorption, and airway aspiration defense for poisonous plants. Aligned with WHO Envenomation Guidelines.

title: Flood-Borne Food Botulism / Spoilage (Profile 4)
trigger_symptoms: ate bulging canned food double vision in evacuation tent
spoiled food weakness swallowing difficulty in evacuation tent
canned rations botulism in evacuation tent
steps: Botulism toxin from bulging/dented flood-damaged cans causes descending muscle paralysis.
Support airway; keep victim sitting upright.
Do not give solid foods.
Document exact cans consumed.
warnings: NEVER eat canned food with bulging lids, leaks, or sour smell in flood disaster.
summary: Descending neuroparalytic botulism airway vigilance and food inspection protocols. Aligned with WHO Envenomation Guidelines.

title: Emergency Chlorine Bleach Water Disinfection (Guideline 1)
trigger_symptoms: purify dirty water with bleach in Sector B
disinfect drinking water flood drops in Sector B
make well water drinkable in Sector B
steps: Ensure bleach is regular, unscented household bleach (5-6% sodium hypochlorite).
For clear water: Add 2 drops of bleach per 1 liter (or 8 drops per gallon).
For cloudy/muddy water: Filter through cloth first, then add 4 drops per liter.
Stir well and let stand for 30 full minutes. Water should have a faint chlorine smell.
If no chlorine smell after 30 min, repeat dose and wait another 15 min.
warnings: NEVER use scented, color-safe, or cleaning bleaches (contains toxic industrial perfumes).
summary: Precision household chlorine bleaching ratio and contact-time validation. Adheres to Sphere Humanitarian Standards.

title: SODIS (Solar Water Disinfection) in PET Plastic Bottles (Guideline 2)
trigger_symptoms: disinfect water with sun bottles in relief shelter 2
solar water purification plastic bottle in relief shelter 2
no fuel boil water sun in relief shelter 2
steps: Filter water through cloth into clear, uncolored PET plastic bottles (under 2 liters).
Shake bottle vigorously for 20 seconds to oxygenate.
Lay bottles flat on a reflective or dark corrugated roof in full midday sun.
Expose to direct sun for minimum 6 consecutive hours (or 2 full days if skies are 50% cloudy).
UV-A radiation and water temperature kill 99.9% of bacteria and viruses.
warnings: DO NOT use glass or PVC bottles (blocks UV-A rays). DO NOT use scratched bottles.
summary: Solar ultraviolet-A disinfection protocol for fuel-depleted disaster zones. Adheres to Sphere Humanitarian Standards.

title: Homemade Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) for Severe Dehydration (Guideline 3)
trigger_symptoms: severe diarrhea dehydration weak in riverbank camp
cholera fluid replacement oral solution in riverbank camp
homemade ORS ratio recipe in riverbank camp
steps: Recipe: Mix exactly 6 level teaspoons of sugar + 0.5 level teaspoon of salt into 1 liter of clean water.
Stir until dissolved. Taste it: should not taste saltier than tears.
Give to adults and children in frequent small sips after every loose stool.
Continue feeding breastmilk or light foods if tolerated.
warnings: DO NOT use too much salt (causes deadly hypernatremia, especially in infants).
summary: Standard WHO oral rehydration salt formula to halt hypovolemic cholera death. Adheres to Sphere Humanitarian Standards.

title: Emergency Field Cat-Hole & Latrine Construction (Guideline 4)
trigger_symptoms: build emergency toilet shelter in water crisis zone
where to defecate in flood camp in water crisis zone
field latrine sanitation in water crisis zone
steps: Locate waste area at least 30 meters (100 feet) away from all water sources, wells, and camp kitchens.
Dig individual cat-hole 6 to 8 inches deep.
After use, cover feces completely with excavated soil to prevent flies from transferring pathogens.
Wash hands with clean water and soap/ash immediately.
warnings: DO NOT defecate directly into floodwaters or within 30m of drinking supplies.
summary: FEMA/Sphere standard 30-meter perimeter disaster sanitation cat-holes. Adheres to Sphere Humanitarian Standards.

title: Emergency Chlorine Bleach Water Disinfection (Guideline 13)

steps: Ensure bleach is regular, unscented household bleach (5-6% sodium hypochlorite).

vomiting and watery stool outbreak in communal hall
steps: Isolate symptomatic individuals in a dedicated tent separated from main shelter.
Designate separate latrine for cholera patients.
Disinfect all vomitus and stools with 2% chlorine solution before disposal.
Provide continuous ORS to prevent vascular collapse.
Enforce handwashing with soap before handling camp food.
warnings: DO NOT mix cholera waste into general camp runoff.
summary: Isolation cohorting and chlorine barrier hygiene for acute cholera control. Complies with WHO Outbreak Response protocols.

title: Tetanus Risk Assessment - Rusty Metal Punctures (Module 2)
trigger_symptoms: stepped on rusty nail in flood water in school gym shelter
deep puncture from corrugated tin sheet in school gym shelter
rusty wire wound dirty in school gym shelter
steps: Wash puncture wound vigorously under running water with soap for 5 minutes.
Encourage slight bleeding to help flush deep contaminants.
Do not seal tightly with glue; cover with breathable dressing.
Identify tetanus toxoid booster status; seek immunization when clinic access returns.
warnings: DO NOT probe deep into puncture wound with unsterilized needles.
summary: Deep irrigation, aerobic drainage, and immunization triage for contaminated punctures. Complies with WHO Outbreak Response protocols.

title: Improvised Emergency Childbirth in Disaster Shelter (Case 1)
trigger_symptoms: woman in labor in shelter baby coming - room 1
crowning baby head visible labor - room 1
emergency birth in evacuation center - room 1
steps: Create clean surface with plastic and towels. Calm the mother.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap.
As baby's head emerges, support gently without pulling.
Dry baby immediately with warm towel to prevent hypothermia; place skin-to-skin on mother's chest.
Tie umbilical cord in two places (at 2 inches and 4 inches from baby) with clean boiled string. Cut between ties with boiled blade.
Encourage immediate breastfeeding to contract uterus and stop bleeding.
warnings: NEVER pull baby's head or shoulders. DO NOT wash off protective vernix grease.
summary: Aseptic field delivery, newborn skin-to-skin thermoregulation, and fundal contraction. Aligned with MSF (Doctors Without Borders) Field Obstetrics.

title: Postpartum Hemorrhage - External Fundal Massage (Case 2)
trigger_symptoms: mother bleeding heavily after birth - barracks 3
postpartum hemorrhage clots soaked sheet - barracks 3
fainting mother after delivery - barracks 3
steps: Bleeding is most often caused by a relaxed, boggy uterus.
Place your hand on mother's lower abdomen just below navel.
Massage uterus firmly with circular downward pressure until it feels hard and firm like a grapefruit.
Put baby to breast immediately (suckling releases natural oxytocin).
Keep mother warm and elevate legs.
warnings: DO NOT stop fundal massage until uterus is firmly contracted.
summary: Bimanual transabdominal fundal massage and nipple suckling stimulation for uterine atony. Aligned with MSF (Doctors Without Borders) Field Obstetrics.

title: Pediatric High Fever & Convulsion Management (Case 3)
trigger_symptoms: toddler burning up shaking febrile seizure - community center
child 104 fever convulsing in shelter - community center
steps: Place child in lateral recovery position on floor away from hard objects.
Sponge forehead and neck with LUKEWARM (not cold) water.
Remove excess heavy clothes.
Once seizure stops, encourage frequent sips of water or ORS.
warnings: NEVER use ice baths or alcohol rubs (triggers shivering and rapid shock).
DO NOT give aspirin to children.
summary: Lukewarm evaporation sponging and febrile seizure airway protection. Aligned with MSF (Doctors Without Borders) Field Obstetrics.

title: Acute Diabetic Hypoglycemia (Low Blood Sugar) (Session 1)
trigger_symptoms: diabetic shaking sweating confused in triage intake
low blood sugar passing out in triage intake
diabetic trembling slurred speech in triage intake
steps: If conscious: Give 15-20 grams of fast-acting sugar immediately (half glass juice, 3-4 sugar cubes, or soda).
If drowsy/unconscious: Rub honey or sugar paste inside their cheek/gums. DO NOT force liquids down throat.
Wait 15 minutes; repeat sugar if symptoms persist.
Follow up with complex carbs (bread or biscuit) once alert.
warnings: DO NOT inject insulin into a hypoglycemic patient (proves rapidly fatal).
